messages:
Sean Gallagher: heads up, need to land on sane defaults for KMS circuit breaker + alerting before we roll past staging. current PR has knobs but we need thresholds that catch partial brownouts without paging us all day. thoughts?

Allison Grant: what metrics do we have / plan to emit? breaker_state, kms_request_latency, kms_error_rate by code? if we can separate throttling vs access denied vs timeouts, alerting can be less noisy.

Emily Zhao: from the implementation side (data plane), the breaker trips on consecutive failures right now. configurable: `kms.cb.failure_threshold` (count), `kms.cb.window_ms`, `kms.cb.open_ms`, retry policy (max attempts, jitter). default draft was 5 failures in 10s -> open for 30s.

Rafael Mendes: 5 in 10s feels too twitchy for multi-tenant noisy neighbors. if one tenant has bad IAM and spams, we’ll open breaker for everyone unless we scope it.

Vikram Singh: +1. breaker needs to be scoped at least per-provider/per-region and ideally per-tenant (or per key-id) if we have that context. otherwise you’ll see false positives during customer misconfig.

Emily Zhao: scope today is per "KMS client" instance (provider+region+credentials), which for Hosted is shared, for Private typically per tenant/customer install. per-tenant in Hosted would be work.

Marcus Lin: from security side: we actually *want* fast signal on AccessDenied / misconfig but don’t want to cascade and take down healthy tenants. can we treat AccessDenied differently than throttles/timeouts?

Kevin Osei: yes please. AccessDenied should be classified as non-retryable (or short retry) and should not trip global breaker. it’s not a dependency brownout, it’s a config issue. also key disabled is distinct.

Allison Grant: alert fatigue concern: if we page on every AccessDenied spike we’ll be paging on customer mistakes all day. recommend:
- page only on systemic signals: timeouts, throttling, 5xx from provider, latency p95/p99 jumps
- create non-paging alert (ticket / slack) for AccessDenied/key disabled with top tenants + key ids

Sean Gallagher: agreed. we’ve been burned by paging on customer IAM denies before.

Rafael Mendes: proposal for paging policy:
1) Page (sev2) when breaker is open AND decrypt failure rate crosses SLO (e.g. >0.25% for 5m) across hosted fleet.
2) Page (sev3) when KMS timeout rate > 2% for 10m OR p95 latency > 2s for 10m, even if decrypt failures not yet high (early brownout).
3) Everything else -> non-paging.

Vikram Singh: for #2: be careful, p95 latency can be high but caching + batching might mask impact. maybe use a "would have called KMS" counter vs actual? though we can approximate with cache miss rate.

Allison Grant: we already have cache hit ratio for decrypt path in the draft metrics. we can condition alerting: only page on high latency if cache_miss_rate is high enough that impact is plausible.

Emily Zhao: we can instrument `kms_cache_hit` and `kms_cache_miss` counters and export breaker trip counts. also add metric tags for `op=Encrypt|Decrypt`.

Connor O'Brien: from release side, we need defaults we can ship behind flag. can we keep breaker conservative in Hosted and more aggressive in Private? (private has fewer tenants and we can control assumptions)

Sean Gallagher: yes, but I’d rather not diverge too much. maybe different paging thresholds, same breaker defaults.

Marcus Lin: question: what’s the failure threshold we should aim for so we don’t keep hammering KMS during outages? security doesn’t want infinite retries + log spam.

Rafael Mendes: breaker open should reduce blast radius by backing off. but opening too fast becomes self-inflicted outage if KMS has transient 429s.

Allison Grant: can we do "adaptive"? e.g. if we see 429s, open quickly but half-open with a low probe rate. if we see timeouts, open slower but for longer.

Emily Zhao: code supports different classifications but doesn’t yet do different open durations by code. we can add later. for now we can set:
- max retry attempts: 3 (with full jitter)
- per-attempt timeout: 750ms (encrypt), 500ms (decrypt)
- breaker: 20 failures in 30s -> open 60s
and count only retryable errors (timeout/5xx/429).

Vikram Singh: 20 failures in 30s might still be quick given call volume. what’s typical QPS to KMS in Hosted with current cache TTL?

Emily Zhao: with cache, steady state is low-ish but during cold start / after deploy, cache miss spikes. we saw ~150-250 req/s to KMS per region during a cold start test.

Sean Gallagher: if KMS is flaking, 20 failures could happen in <1s. that might be fine; opening for 60s may be too long if it was a 2s blip though.

Rafael Mendes: compromise: 50 failures in 30s -> open 15s, then half-open. plus exponential backoff on open state probes.

Allison Grant: alerting side, breaker_open for 15s is not worth paging. page only if breaker_open persists >5m OR flaps (opens > X times in 10m) AND we see user impact.

Kevin Osei: +1, paging on breaker state alone will be noisy. impact signal should be decrypt failures at service boundary.

Marcus Lin: also audit events will include kms failures; we need to be careful not to flood audit pipeline during an outage. consider sampling for repeated identical errors while breaker open.

Vikram Singh: sampling in audit seems good but separate track. for now, service logs should aggregate. metrics should be enough.

Sean Gallagher: ok, let’s nail this down:
- breaker counts only retryable errors (timeouts, throttles/429, provider 5xx)
- AccessDenied/DisabledKey => no retries beyond 1, no breaker increment
- breaker threshold: 50 failures / 30s, open 15s
- half-open: allow 1 request per 1s (or 5% of normal?)
- alerts:
  a) page if decrypt_failure_rate >0.25% for 5m OR >1% for 1m (fast burn)
  b) page if kms_timeout_rate >2% for 10m AND cache_miss_rate >20%
  c) non-paging: sustained AccessDenied >N/min with top tenants + key ids
sound right?

Allison Grant: mostly. for (b) add p95 latency >2s as alternate condition, since timeouts might not capture brownout. we can do "(timeout_rate>2% OR p95>2s)".

Rafael Mendes: also add flap detector: breaker_open_count > 10 in 10m with elevated KMS errors -> create incident in #incidents but not page? maybe page only if user impact.

Connor O'Brien: can we put these in the rollout checklist? I want explicit: what dashboards to check in canary.

Sean Gallagher: yep, will add to release checklist thread and to the runbook doc. Allison can you draft alert rules in the alerting review doc?

Allison Grant: yes. I’ll draft Grafana panels + alert expressions today. will tag you and Rafael for review.

Emily Zhao: I’ll update config defaults in the PR and split error classifications. will need review from Vikram for perf impact.

Vikram Singh: happy to review. pls include a load test note: worst-case added latency when breaker half-open.

Marcus Lin: please also ensure we log which key-id/alias (sanitized) for AccessDenied so we can triage with customers.

Kevin Osei: +1 and keep it consistent with audit event schema (key_ref, provider, region, error_code). even if we don’t emit full audit on every failure, the metric tags should exist.

Sean Gallagher: cool. action items:
- Emily: update breaker defaults + classification + half-open probes
- Allison: alert draft + dashboards
- Rafael: add to game day scenarios: partial throttling (429) in one region + validate no pager unless impact
- Connor: fold into release checklist
we’ll re-check after staging chaos run.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: also recommend we test "slow KMS" (p95 3-5s) not just hard errors. that’s the real brownout.

Allison Grant: ack. I’ll include a synthetic panel for "kms_call_duration" with percentiles and overlay breaker state.

Sean Gallagher: thanks all. closing loop after the next chaos run.
